# Design requirements (version 0.3.0)

Design requirements from the v3 brief, Section 3. Each traces to a finding; DR IDs are used in the provenance fields of the other content files.

| ID | Finding | Source | Design requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| DR1 | Educator capacity, not technology, appears to be the binding constraint | Study 1, Tier 3; Discussion | The platform targets educators, not students, and treats capacity as institutionally conditioned. |
| DR2 | Standards specifying student outcomes without institutional conditions act as exhortation | Study 1 Conclusion | Profile institutional conditions alongside individual practice (A3). |
| DR3 | The only controlled study testing explainable AI in novice clinicians found automation bias | Study 1, Tier 4 [AYMAN TO SUPPLY: Table 1 ID] | Scenario SC1; the coach invites critique of its own output (A7). |
| DR4 | The only RCT in the corpus found no transfer of AI training to unaided performance | Study 1, Tier 4 [AYMAN TO SUPPLY: Table 1 ID] | Scenario SC2; practice evidence asks about performance without the tool (A6). |
| DR5 | Foundational AI literacy has the most defensible evidence base; applied clinical competencies do not yet | Study 1 Conclusion | Coach and scenarios prioritise literacy-level change and avoid overclaiming applied outcomes (A7, SC4). |
| DR6 | No included intervention reached behaviour change in practice or patient outcomes | Study 1, outcome-level analysis | The platform captures enacted practice and its consequences, not only attitudes (A6). |
| DR7 | The risk of ceremonial compliance under accreditation pressure | Meyer and Rowan (1977); Study 2 Theme 2 (documentation) | No certificates; a decoupling probe item; scenario SC3 (A3, A6). |
| DR8 | Design must be revisable from Studies 2–3 and the Delphi | DBR methodology chapter | All content in versioned data files with provenance (A1). |
